claim: For Matsuno's Algorithm 2, set eta=1/10 and start at B=(1,-5) in the triangle with other vertices A=(1,-50) and C=(2,50). For every tolerance epsilon>0 the algorithm never stops, though the origin is strictly outside the triangle. It selects C and A alternately with old-point weight 9/10, approaching (28/19,-50/19) and (29/19,50/19) by parity with exact two-step factor 81/100. The visited vertices share a minimizing face with negative support; the example is consistent with Theorem 3.2's face-distance decay.
integrity: Exact rational inequalities prove forward invariance and nontermination; the cycle follows from the affine two-step map. The accompanying arithmetic checker covers the rational bounds and identities, not the scope of Theorem 3.2.
scientific_limitations: One admissible eta, one triangle and one starting vertex; no classification of other inputs.
The two selected vertices are on the same minimizing face. That face has negative support, so its distance decay does not certify a separating normal. The example does not violate Theorem 3.2.
title: A fixed move floor creates an attracting two-cycle in the Naive Separation Algorithm
